source_text: Ὅτι δὲ καὶ ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν γενόμενος ἄνθρωπος παθεῖν καὶ ἀτιμασθῆναι ὑπέμεινε καὶ πάλιν μετὰ δόξης παραγενήσεται, ἀκούσατε τῶν εἰρημένων εἰς τοῦτο προφητειῶν. Ἔστι δὲ ταῦτα· „Ἀνθ᾿ ὧν παρέδωκαν εἰς θάνατον τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ, καὶ μετὰ τῶν ἀνόμων ἐλογίσθη, αὐτὸς ἁμαρτίας πολλῶν εἴληφε καί τοῖς ἀνόμοις ἐξιλάσεται. Ἴδε γὰρ συνήσει ὁ παῖς μου, καὶ ὑψωθήσεται καὶ δοξασθήσεται σφόδρα. Ὃν τρόπον ἐκστήσονται πολλοὶ ἐπὶ σέ, οὕτως ἀδοξήσει ἀπὸ ἀνθρώπων τὸ εἶδός σου καὶ ἡ δόξα σου ἀπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων, οὕτως θαυμάσονται ἔθνη πολλά, καὶ συνέξουσι βασιλεῖς τὸ στόμα αἰτῶν· ὅτι οἷς οὐκ ἀνηγγέλη περὶ αὐτοῦ ὄψονται, καὶ οἳ οὐκ ἀκηκόασι συνήσουσι. Κύριε, τίς ἐπίστευσε τῇ ἀκοῇ ἡμῶν; καὶ ὁ βραχίων κυρίου τίνι ἀπεκαλύφθη; Ἀνηγγείλαμεν ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ ὡς παιδίον, ὡς ῥίζα ἐν γῇ διψώσῃ. Οὐκ ἔστιν εἶδος αὐτῷ οὐδὲ δέξα· καὶ εἴδομεν αὐτόν, καὶ οὐκ εἶχεν εἶδος οὐδὲ κάλλος, ἀλλὰ τὸ εἶδος αὐτοῦ ἄτιμον καὶ ἐκλεῖπον παρὰ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους. Ἄνθρωπος ἐν πληγῇ ὢν καὶ εἰδὼς φέρειν μαλακίαν, ὅτι ἀπέστραπται τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ, ἠτιμάσθη καὶ οὐκ ἐλογίσθη. Οὗτος τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν φέρει καὶ περὶ ἡμῶν ὀδυνᾶται, καὶ ἡμεῖς ἐλογισάμεθα αὐτὸν εἶναι ἐν πόνῳ καὶ ἐν πληγῇ καὶ ἐν κακώσει. Αὐτὸς δὲ ἐτραυματίσθη διὰ τὰς ἀνομίας ἡμῶν καὶ μεμαλάκισται διὰ τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν· παιδεία εἰρήνης ἐπ᾿ αὐτόν, τῷ μώλωπι αἰτοῦ ἡμεῖς ἰάθημεν. Πάντες ὡς πρόβατα ἐπλανήθημεν, ἄνθρωπος τῇ ὁδῷ αὐτοῦ ἐπλανήθη· καὶ παρέδωκεν αὐτὸν ταῖς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν, καὶ αὐτὸς διὰ τὸ κεκακῶσθαι οὐκ ἀνοίγει τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ. Ὡς πρόβατον ἐπὶ σφαγὴν ἤχθη, καὶ ὡς ἀμνὸς ἐναντίον τοῦ κείροντος αὐτὸν ἄφωνος, οὕτως οὐκ ἀνοίγει τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ. Ἐν τῇ ταπεινώσει αὐτοῦ ἡ κρίσις αὐτοῦ ἤρθη“. Μετὰ οἶν τὸ σταυρωθῆναι αὐτὸν καὶ οἱ γνώριμοι αὐτοῦ πάντες ἀπέστησαν, ἀρνησάμενοι αὐτόν· ὕστερον δέ, ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστάντος καὶ ὀφθέντος αὐτοῖς καὶ ταῖς προφητείαις ἐντυχεῖν, ἐν αἷς πάντα ταῦτα προείρητο γενησόμενα, διδάξαντος, καὶ εἰς οὐρανὸν ἀνερχόμενον ἰδόντες καὶ πιστεύσαντες καὶ δύναμιν ἐκεῖθεν αἰτοῖς πεμφθεῖσαν παρ᾿ αὐτοῦ λαβόντες καὶ εἰς πᾶν γένος ἀνθρώπων ἐλθόντες, ταῦτα ἐδίδαξαν καὶ ἀπόστολοι προσηγορεύθησαν.
pass_a_gloss: That also having become a man he endured to suffer and be dishonored and again with glory he will come, hear the prophecies spoken to this effect. There are these: 'Instead of which they delivered his soul to death and he was reckoned with the lawless, he himself bore the sins of many and he will propitiate the lawless. For my servant will understand and he will be exalted and greatly glorified. Just as many will be astonished at you, so your appearance will be dishonored among men and your glory among men, so many nations will marvel and kings will shut their mouths in petition; for those to whom it was not reported about him will see and those who have not heard will understand.' 'Lord, who has believed our report? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed? We reported before him as a child, as a root in dry ground. There is no appearance to him nor comeliness; and we saw him and he had no appearance nor beauty, but his appearance was dishonored and lacking among men.' 'A man in suffering being and knowing weakness, because his face was turned away, he was dishonored and not reckoned. This one bears our sins and suffers on our behalf and we reckoned him to be in labor and in suffering and in evil. But he was wounded because of our lawlessness and bruised because of our sins; a discipline of peace is upon him, by his bruise we were healed. All we like sheep went astray, a man in his way went astray; and he delivered him to our sins and he because of the evil done to him does not open his mouth. Like a sheep to slaughter he was led and like a lamb before his shearer silent, so he does not open his mouth. In his humiliation his judgment was taken away.' After he was crucified and all who knew him denied him, having renounced him; but later, having risen from the dead and appeared to them and having encountered the prophecies in which all these things were spoken as going to happen, having taught, and having seen him going up into heaven and having believed and having received power sent from there by him and having come to every nation of men, they taught these things and were called apostles.

choices.why: literal translation of παιδεία and εἰρήνης
literal translation of ἐν and ταπεινώσει

pass_b_english: Because he became a man for our sake, endured suffering and dishonor, and will return again in glory, listen to the prophecies spoken to this effect. These are they: 'Because they handed his life over to death, and he was counted among the lawless, he himself bore the sins of many and will make atonement for the lawless.' 'For my servant will understand, and he will be exalted and greatly glorified.' 'Just as many were astonished at you, so your appearance will be dishonored among men and your glory among men; so many nations will marvel, and kings will shut their mouths in petition, for those to whom it was not reported about him will see, and those who have not heard will understand.' 'Lord, who has believed our report? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?' 'We announced him before him like a child, like a root in dry ground.' 'He has no appearance or comeliness; we saw him, and he had no appearance or beauty, but his appearance was dishonored and lacking among men.' 'A man in suffering and acquainted with weakness, because his face was turned away, he was dishonored and not reckoned.' 'This one bears our sins and suffers on our behalf, and we reckoned him to be in labor, in suffering, and in affliction.' 'But he was wounded because of our lawlessness and bruised because of our sins; a discipline of peace is upon him, and by his bruise we were healed.' 'All of us like sheep went astray, a man went astray in his own way; and he delivered him to our sins, and he, because of the evil done to him, does not open his mouth.' 'Like a sheep he was led to slaughter, and like a lamb before its shearer is silent, so he does not open his mouth.' 'In his humiliation his judgment was taken away.' After he was crucified, all who knew him deserted him, denying him; but later, after he rose from the dead, appeared to them, and they encountered the prophecies in which all these things were foretold as going to happen, having been taught, and after they saw him ascending into heaven, believed, and received power sent from there by him, and went out to every nation of men, they taught these things and were called apostles.
